particularites.text: HCSS acquisition consolidated from 1 July 2026: generates RECURRING PPA amortisation on the identified intangible assets (customer relationships, technology), at a roughly CONSTANT amount in euros over its life (a charge that does not decline as such - on the contrary, the 2026 effect covers only one half-year of consolidation, that of 2027 a full year, hence higher in absolute terms). The NET effect on EPS (dilutive in 2026, neutral in 2027, accretive from 2028 according to management) comes from the organic growth of HCSS earnings catching up with and then exceeding that stable charge - not from the amortisation itself disappearing. On top of that, 2026 carries a one-off (non-recurring) haircut on deferred revenue written down in purchase accounting, concentrated in the second half. [20/08/2026: valuePct removed from the expected return - the PPA/HCSS effect is ALREADY carried by the Omnium EPS trajectory (GAAP basis, amortisation retained); counting it in 'special items' at -3%/yr double-counted the charge and distorted the Expected return.]

clesRetenues: Q George Webb (Morgan Stanley) - Bluebeam Max adoption and the weight of the Media segment: rollout 'better than expected' with strong customer feedback on productivity gains; Media weakness comes from customer consolidation and M&A in the sector, not from disruption by generative AI - Media guidance cut to mid-single-digit growth.

Q George Webb (Morgan Stanley) - HCSS revenue bridge: contribution expected above 80 M€ in H2 26 (before purchase accounting), deferred revenue haircut estimated at between 20 and 30 M€ over 12 months and concentrated at the start of the period; EPS accretion trajectory: dilutive in 2026, neutral in 2027, accretive in 2028 (or 2027 if the conservative assumptions are relaxed).

Q Alice Jennings (Barclays) - implications of the growth slowdown in H2: 16% growth in H1 (constant currency) supports confidence in the 14-15% annual guidance; cautious positioning given macro uncertainty, no guidance revision by segment other than Media; investment priorities unchanged (product, AI, venture capital, M&A screening).

Q Nicolas David (Oddo BHF) - assumptions on multi-year contracts and transactional FX effect: multi-year contracts expected at a similar level in H2 vs H1, with no additional headwind/tailwind; extraordinary FX effect in Q2 due to the Hungarian forint (sharp appreciation after the April elections), generating a transactional revaluation loss in a subsidiary holding euro-denominated assets.

Q Nicolas David (Oddo BHF) - momentum in Germany: positive dynamic driven by the digitalisation of building permits and the stabilisation of residential; Bluebeam and Design are performing well in the German market.

Q Naiso Nining (Berenberg) - AI monetisation strategy outside Bluebeam: planned launch of premium 'Max' tiers on other ranges (ALLPLAN Max, Steel Genie); hybrid consumption-based (token) models considered over the medium term but priority given to subscription for near-term adoption; ~70% of the architects surveyed express reservations about trusting AI outputs in general.

Q Joseph George (JP Morgan) - organic growth trajectory of the Build segment post-HCSS integration: Build expected close to 20% organic growth one year after full integration, Bluebeam above 20%, HCSS at the top of the teens range (high teens).

Q Victor Cheng (Bank of America) - HCSS growth in H1 and the H2 bridge; Design's transition to subscription: HCSS growing strongly at high teens in H1 with no marked seasonality; deferred purchase accounting effects concentrated in H1, lower in H2; Design now at 65% subscription (target 70% at end-2026, above 90% at end-2027) - a transition creating a drag through 2027, price growth driven by new AI features rather than by pure price increases.

Q Michael Briest (UBS) - acquisition price and contribution of ComputerWorks: answer truncated in the sources available for this refresh, to be completed if a more complete transcript becomes accessible.

Q (multi-year contracts and M&A impact on guidance) - multi-year contracts providing a tailwind of a few million euros in Q1, similar to 2025; organic guidance confirmed, some M&A costs in Q1, further details expected after the closing of the HCSS acquisition.

Q (Middle East geopolitical impact and Media outlook) - limited regional exposure; Media segment expected to grow at a high single-digit rate in 2026, revised down from the previous expectation of double-digit growth.

Q (reseller acquisition strategy) - objective of controlling go-to-market and the customer relationship; the resellers acquired often have their own intellectual property and localisation, with contracts varying between commission and revenue sharing.

Q (Build segment growth and cross-selling) - Build maintains solid double-digit growth, above 20% expected for 2026; cross-selling between Bluebeam and GoCanvas improving with a growing customer base.

Q (AI monetisation strategy) - monetisation dependent on the product/features; Bluebeam Max on subscription with potential consumption-based (token) pricing, a model that could be applied to the Design segment.

Quantified context for the quarter: reported revenue +10,7% to 313,1 M€ (+17% at constant currency), ARR +14,4% reported (+21% at constant currency, ~1,2 Md€), EBITDA margin at 31,4%, EBITDA +22% reported (~+30% at constant currency) to 98,4 M€, EPS 0,52€.

dernierCall.guidanceProchainTrimestre: No quarterly guidance (the company guides on a full-year basis). Management flagged an expected H2 growth deceleration versus the +16% cc achieved in H1, due to tough Build comparables (GoCanvas contribution and post-Bluebeam-transition effects in 2025); no additional multi-year contract effect is assumed in H2 and Media is expected around mid-single-digit growth.
dernierCall.guidanceAnnuelle: FY26 organic guidance fully confirmed: revenue growth of 14-15% cc (CEO referenced 14-16% in the Q&A and sees the group tracking well after +16% cc in H1) and EBITDA margin of 32-33%, close to 33% excluding acquisition-related one-off costs. HCSS, consolidated from July 1, 2026, adds around 600bps of cc revenue growth in FY26 after the estimated PPA effect and dilutes the reported EBITDA margin by around 150bps (PPA, integration costs and a new share-based compensation program for the enlarged Build segment); the front-loaded IFRS deferred-revenue haircut reduces the H2 26 HCSS contribution by a mid-to-high EUR 20s million amount. Guidance assumes no material macro deterioration and the HCSS financial impact remains preliminary until the PPA is finalized later this year.
pointsCles: H1 26 revenue up 11.9% reported (+15.7% cc) to EUR 640.7m, Q2 up 13% reported (+14.5% cc) despite a very high comparison base; Q2 EBITDA of EUR 98.6m for a 30.1% reported margin, depressed by an extraordinary transactional FX effect (higher single-digit EUR m) and HCSS deal costs - 31% excluding deal costs - while Q2 net income rose 20.3% to EUR 66m (IFRS EPS EUR 0.57).

Subscription/SaaS revenue grew 32.4% cc in H1 to EUR 514.7m, lifting recurring revenue to a record 95% of group sales (subscription/SaaS at 80%) and ARR to EUR 1.25bn (+17.4% cc); perpetual licenses are down 40.8% cc and now only 2% of group revenue.

Segments diverged: Build stayed the engine (+27.1% cc in H1, 39.8% EBITDA margin, +520bps yoy) while Design grew 9.7% cc mid-transition (65% of Design revenue in subscription at end-Q2, ~70% targeted for end-2026, 90%+ by end-2027, tailwind only from 2028) and Media disappointed (+3.3% cc) on US media & entertainment customer consolidation, with Maxon cut to mid-single-digit growth for 2026.

HCSS, the group's largest-ever acquisition, is consolidated from July 1, 2026: underlying growth kept in the higher teens, H2 26 revenue contribution seen clearly above EUR 80m after a front-loaded IFRS deferred-revenue haircut (mid-to-high EUR 20s m), and EPS framed as dilutive in 2026, roughly flat in 2027 and clearly accretive in 2028 (~28% minority stake held by Thoma Bravo).

hypothese.summary: German design/construction software vendor (Design/Build/Manage/Media), in a structural SaaS transition with ARR and margin expanding continuously; the HCSS acquisition (July 2026) broadens the Build segment but transitorily dilutes EPS ahead of the accretion expected in 2028.
hypothese.text:
== THESIS SUMMARY ==
Founder-family-controlled (~51%) design/build software house in structural transition to subscription/SaaS: recurring revenue hit 80% of group in Q2 26 (record), Design targeting >90% by end-2027. The transition drives continuous margin expansion (EBITDA 25.0% in 2021 -> 31.2% in 2025) while transiently braking reported growth during the maintenance-to-subscription switch. HCSS (US infrastructure software) adds ~600bp reported growth and dilutes margin ~150bp during integration. FY26 guidance reaffirmed at Q2: organic +14/15% cc, organic EBITDA margin 32-33%.

== THESIS READ ==
- Transition executing on plan - 80% recurring is the proof point; the reported-growth brake is temporary by construction. Watch: Design segment recurring share vs the >90% end-2027 target.
- HCSS integration is the main new-money risk (debt-funded, ~460M net debt 2026). Watch: HCSS growth retention and deleveraging pace.
- 2027+ net conversion (~78% of EBIT) embeds a below-EBIT tailwind vs a flat 25% ETR - consensus-derived net, documented in the bridge 'other' line. Watch: arbitrate at next refresh with full statements.

== SPECIAL FACTORS ==
Fiche created at Q2 26: historical net debt 2021-2024 estimated by qualitative cross-check (only hard point: ~8M net debt at Q1 26); quarterly EPS Q3/Q4 26 and 2027 are estimates on consensus + 2025 seasonality. priorEPS null by construction (no earlier vintage exists). Basis: management non-GAAP excludes PPA amortization; Omnium tracks GAAP consensus.

== PARAMETERS & WATCH-LIST ==
2026: revenue 1,435M (organic mid + HCSS), EBIT 352M, net 262M (GAAP consensus-aligned). 2027-2030: ~13%/yr revenue, margin expansion, deleveraging to net cash by 2030. Bridge: ETR 25%; the 'other' line carries the consensus conversion wedge (to arbitrate). Watch: Q3 26 (first post-creation print); HCSS disclosure granularity; historical nd correction from annual reports.

== CATALYSTS ==
Q3 26 (Oct); HCSS first full-quarter disclosures; Design recurring-share milestones; FY27 guidance (Mar).

ancrages.moteur: Consolidation of HCSS from 1 July 2026: around 600 basis points of reported revenue growth added in the second half of 2026 and over the full year 2027, with a transitory dilutive effect on the EBIT margin (PPA amortisation, deferred revenue haircut) that gradually fades until the accretion expected in 2028.

Structural SaaS transition under way: subscription/SaaS at 80% of group revenue in Q2 26 (a record), with Design targeting more than 90% of its revenue on subscription by end-2027 - a rising recurring mix that supports margin expansion beyond the HCSS effect alone.

Build segment (Bluebeam + HCSS) expected close to 20% organic growth one year after the full integration of HCSS according to management, driven by Bluebeam (above 20%) and HCSS (top of the teens range).

Balance sheet carrying very little debt ahead of HCSS (near-zero net debt, around 8 M€ in Q1 26); the HCSS acquisition, debt-financed (estimated impact of around 450 M€ on net debt), temporarily weakens leverage, but rapid deleveraging is expected given the group's historical cash generation (operating cash flow +31,3% in 2025).

Stable family control (around 51% aggregate Nemetschek/foundations) since the 1999 IPO - long-term-oriented governance, consistent with the targeted product/AI/M&A investment strategy reaffirmed in Q2 26.
